guides.title: Birth, marriage, and death certificates
guides.scope: Provincial information or national service available to Siquijor residents
guides.content:
# Birth, marriage, and death certificates

Request a PSA birth, marriage, or death certificate. Find the details to prepare, application steps, delivery options, and fees below.

## Which information should you prepare?

Have the following record details ready before starting your request. Identity and authorization checks apply when the certificate is released.

### Birth certificate

- Child’s full name, including middle name.
- Father’s full name and mother’s full maiden name.
- Birth date and municipality/city and province of birth.
- Whether registration was late and, if so, the year it was registered.
- Requester’s full name, address, and relationship to the child.
- Number of copies and the reason for the request. [1]

### Marriage certificate

Prepare both spouses’ full names, the marriage date and place, your own full name and address, the quantity needed, and the request’s purpose. [2]

### Death certificate

Prepare the deceased person’s full name, date and place of death, your own complete name and address, the quantity needed, and the request’s purpose. The national page additionally lists the place of marriage among its death-request fields; use the actual issuing channel’s form to establish whether that field applies. [3]

## How to request a certificate

1. Identify the certificate and gather its record details above.
2. Choose an **in-person PSA outlet request** or an **online delivery request**. PSA’s birth-certificate page says an appointment is required for walk-in requests. Its linked appointment service is `appointment.psa.gov.ph`. PSA identifies **PSA Serbilis** and **PSAHelpline** as online channels. [1]
3. Give your real requester and record details to the chosen official channel. Birth records have restricted release; the PSA page lists the record owner, authorized persons, and specified relatives or legal representatives among those who may request them. [1]
4. Follow that channel’s identity/authorization checks and retain its reference or receipt. For an outlet transaction, follow the release instruction on your receipt rather than assume same-day release.

For online submission, PSA’s listed channels are [PSA Serbilis](https://www.psaserbilis.com.ph/) and [PSAHelpline](https://psahelpline.ph/).

## PSA Serbilis fees for Philippine delivery and related channels

The provider’s published FAQ lists these charges. The figures are for **PSA Serbilis**, not a universal PSA outlet or PSAHelpline price. The FAQ is undated; the figures below were checked on **17 November 2026**. [4]

| Receiving option | Birth, marriage, or death | CENOMAR or CENODEATH |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First copy: Philippine door delivery, LBC pickup, or embassy delivery | ₱330 | ₱430 |
| Each additional copy under its published tiered-pricing example | ₱280 | ₱380 |
| Government-agency E-Copy | ₱300 | ₱360 |
| Viewable Online | ₱130 | ₱185 |

**Viewable Online** is paid at a PSA CRS outlet for identity verification and an access code. Its optional **DocPrint** paper copy is **₱80 per copy**, requested within the online document’s **60-day** validity. Government-agency E-Copy and Viewable Online are separate receiving options; they are not the same as paper courier delivery. [4]

## Delivery to Siquijor

Siquijor falls under the provider’s **Other Provinces** destination category. Its delivery page estimates **6–8 working days** for that category, with **5–7 additional days** outside the courier’s standard service areas. It asks customers to allow **10–15 additional working days** for requests requiring manual PSA searching. Flight unavailability or cancellation can alter the schedule. These are provider estimates, not a fixed Siquijor island delivery guarantee. [5]

The request’s receiving option and address determine the total shown before payment. A certificate order is a different transaction from a correction, late registration, or marriage-license application at the relevant civil registrar.

## Sources and dates

1. [PSA — Birth Certificate (undated service page)](https://psa.gov.ph/birth-certificate)
2. [PSA — Marriage Certificate (undated service page)](https://psa.gov.ph/marriage-certificate)
3. [PSA — Death Certificate (undated service page)](https://psa.gov.ph/death-certificate)
4. [PSA Serbilis — Frequently Asked Questions, Payment and Viewable Online sections (undated)](https://www.psaserbilis.com.ph/GetFaQs)
5. [PSA Serbilis — Delivery schedule (undated)](https://psaserbilis.com.ph/Delivery)

# National ID registration and Digital National ID

Register for your National ID or download a Digital National ID if you are already registered. Find the steps and fee information below.

## If you are already registered with PhilSys

To access your Digital National ID: [1]

1. Use a computer or smartphone with internet and a camera for the facial verification step.
2. Open the official Digital National ID service at `national-id.gov.ph`.
3. Choose **Proceed** and review the consent for using identity information and the facial image to authenticate you.
4. Enter your first, middle, and last names and date of birth, then continue.
5. Start the **liveness** check and follow the facial-verification instructions.
6. After successful verification, display your National ID and use the download option to retain a personal copy.

You must already be registered with PhilSys to retrieve a Digital National ID. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete identity verification.

## Fees and timing

**Assisted Digital National ID generation is free.** The **2025 PSA charter** sets a **seven-minute** service standard, subject to internet connectivity. Allow time for queuing and identity verification. First-time registration and plastic-card delivery follow separate processes. [2]

## If you have never registered

PSA’s registration notice says its old online Step 1 registration service is disabled and applicants may register in person at a PhilSys registration center with supporting documents. [3] A Digital National ID download cannot substitute for that registration.

Bring your supporting identity documents to a PhilSys registration center. Contact PSA before travelling to check the center’s schedule and documents for your circumstances.

## Access your Digital National ID

[Digital National ID access](https://national-id.gov.ph/) is the official retrieval service. BetterSiquijor does not ask for your date of birth, take your photo, or run the biometric check.

## Sources and dates

1. [PSA RSSO VIII — Digital National ID instructions, 9 August 2024](https://rsso08.psa.gov.ph/content/digital-national-id-now-downloadable-all-filipinos-registered-philsys)
2. [PSA — 2025 Citizen’s Charter, PhilSys Registry Office external services](https://psa.gov.ph/system/files/citizens-charter/5-PSA-2025-Citizens-Charter-Philippine-Identification-System-Registry%20Office-External-Services.pdf)

# PhilHealth registration and member services

Register with PhilHealth, access your Member Data Record, or manage your membership online. Find the steps and Siquijor office contact below.

## Choose the transaction that matches your situation

| Situation | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Employed, no PhilHealth Identification Number (PIN) yet | Complete two PMRF copies and submit them to your employer’s HR unit; await the Member Data Record (MDR) and ID through the employer. [1] |
| Newly hired, already has a PIN | Give the existing PIN to the employer for employee reporting. [1] |
| Applying under PhilHealth’s informal-economy procedure | Submit two completed PMRF copies to a Local Health Insurance Office or PhilHealth Express and await the MDR and ID. The published procedure also covers payment using the assigned number. [2] |
| Already registered and needs records online | Create or use a Member Portal account. [3–4] |

Use your existing PIN if you already have one. Choose the procedure that matches your membership category.

## Existing-member portal: what to prepare

The account-creation screen asks for a **PIN, names, birth date, sex, email address, mobile number, and a chosen password**. It provides a mononym option. The password requirements shown are **8–32 characters**, with a digit, upper- and lowercase letters, and a special character. Complete its CAPTCHA and account-creation action. [4]

For later login, the portal requests the PIN, password, and CAPTCHA. A password-reset request asks for the **PIN and email address** and sends a reset link. [5]

PhilHealth lists online access to contribution records and the MDR, premium payment, and YAKAP clinic selection among member services. Those functions do not themselves determine a particular patient’s benefit entitlement. [3]

## Visit or contact PhilHealth Siquijor

**Ground Floor, Multi-Purpose Center, Poblacion, Siquijor 6225, Siquijor**. Contact: **(035) 480-9844**, **0975 241 6827**, **satelliteofficesiquijor.pro7@philhealth.gov.ph**. [6]

## Manage your membership

Use the agency’s [Member Portal](https://memberinquiry.philhealth.gov.ph/member/) for an online transaction or the proper employer/PhilHealth office for registration. Submit membership details and payments directly to PhilHealth or your employer, as applicable.

## Sources and dates

2. [PhilHealth — Informal Economy Registration Procedures](https://www.philhealth.gov.ph/members/informal/registration.php)

# Basic education enrollment in Siquijor

Enroll a learner in basic education. Prepare the enrollment form and supporting documents, then submit them to the learner’s school.

[Find a school near you](/services/education/find-school).

## Who handles enrollment?

The learner’s school receives the enrollment documents. The Schools Division of Siquijor’s published office is **Helen, Larena, Siquijor**; its email is **deped.siquijor@deped.gov.ph** and published mobile is **0906 432 9162**. [1]

## How to enroll

DepEd’s **13 June 2025 Revised Basic Education Enrollment Policy** and its following-day public explainer describe these arrangements: [2–3]

1. Complete the **Basic Education Enrollment Form (BEEF)** and submit it with the applicable supporting documents to the school.
2. For a minor, the enrollment form is signed by a parent or legal guardian; an adult learner may submit their own enrollment.
3. The policy calls for the original or certified true copy of a PSA/NSO birth certificate, submitted **once across K–12**. Where it is unavailable, the published policy allows specified secondary documents, including a National ID, local certificate of live birth, barangay certification, or a parent-signed undertaking. The **2025 explainer** refers to **31 October** for temporary secondary-document acceptance; this guide does not present that as a new 2026 deadline.
4. Enrollment can be conducted in person or using the school’s designated remote submission arrangements, such as email, messaging, or a drop box.
5. For a transfer, school records are transmitted **school to school** rather than treated as a new parent-printed requirement.

## Fees and school-year dates

The **2025 DepEd explainer** states that voluntary fees are not collected during early registration and enrollment. This is not a claim that every school-related purchase or private-school tuition is free.

## Before you contact the school

Have the learner’s name, grade level, existing Learner Reference Number if applicable, and school ready when you ask about enrollment. Ask the school to identify its currently accepted submission method before sending personal documents.

## Sources and dates

1. [Schools Division of Siquijor — Division Office](https://www.deped-siquijor.com/districts/)
2. [DepEd Order 017, s. 2025 — Revised Basic Education Enrollment Policy, 13 June 2025](https://www.deped.gov.ph/2025/06/13/june-13-2025-do-017-s-2025-revised-basic-education-enrollment-policy/)
3. [DepEd — Revised enrollment policy explainer, 14 June 2025](https://www.deped.gov.ph/2025/06/14/deped-may-mas-pinadali-at-mas-abot-kayang-enrollment-sa-ilalim-ng-pbbm-admin/)

guides.scope: Provincial information or national service available to Siquijor residents
guides.content:
# Request school records

Get a School Form 9, Good Moral Certificate, or Certificate of Enrollment from the learner’s school. Requirements and service standards below follow **DepEd’s 2026 Citizen’s Charter, 2nd Edition**. [1]

[Find your school’s location and contact details](/services/education/find-school).

## Documents to bring

- A request letter signed by the parent or guardian, stating the learner’s SF9 request: **one original and one photocopy**.
- A government-issued valid ID: **one original and one photocopy**.
- If using an authorized representative: **one original authorization letter** and **one photocopy of the requesting person’s government-issued valid ID**.

Examples of IDs listed in the charter include PhilSys ID/ePhilID, Philippine passport, driver’s license, PRC ID, UMID, voter’s ID, senior citizen ID, postal ID, PhilHealth ID, and barangay ID. [1]

## How to request

1. Submit the required documents to the school registrar or records custodian.
2. The school checks the request, verifies the record, and prepares the document for signature.
3. Wait for the school’s release notice.
4. Claim your document and sign the school’s release log.

## Fees and processing time

| Document | Fee | Charter service standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| School Form 9 | None | 59 minutes |
| Good Moral Certificate or Certificate of Enrollment | None | 54 minutes |

These are the charter’s processing standards for the specified services. Ask the school about the availability of the learner’s record and collection arrangements. [1]

## Academic records for local employment

Past learners requesting certified SF9 or SF10 for local employment should bring **one original request letter** and a **government-issued valid ID, original plus one photocopy**. An authorized representative also needs an original authorization letter and a photocopy of the requesting person’s government-issued valid ID. The charter lists **no fee** and a **3-hour, 59-minute** service standard. [1]

## Contact the Schools Division

**Helen, Larena, Siquijor**  
**0906 432 9162**  
**deped.siquijor@deped.gov.ph** [2]

For enrollment, see [Enroll in basic education](/services/education/schools-division).

[Download DepEd’s 2026 charter (PDF, approximately 10 MB)](/documents/deped-citizens-charter-2026-2nd-edition.pdf).

## Sources and dates

guides.title: Siquijor destination guide
guides.scope: Verified destinations across all six municipalities, heritage sites, marine sanctuaries, and festivals
guides.content:
# Siquijor destination guide

Explore Siquijor’s waterfalls, heritage churches, marine sanctuaries, caves, mountain forest reserve, and annual festivals across all six municipalities.

Siquijor is part of the **Negros Island Region (NIR)** and is promoted by the Department of Tourism as the **Healing Island** for its traditional wellness heritage and natural sites. [1]

## Destinations by municipality

### Siquijor (Capital Town)

- **St. Francis of Assisi Church & Bell Tower** (Poblacion) — Built in 1774, the oldest church on the island, with a separate bell tower that historically served as a watchtower. [2, 6]
- **Mt. Bandilaan Nature Park / Siquijor Forest Reserve** (Cang-agong; extends into Lazi) — Established under **Proclamation No. 523, s. 1940** (212 hectares). Siquijor’s highest peak at **557 m**, featuring a 5-storey viewing tower, Way of the Cross trail, watershed forest, habitat of the endemic streak-breasted bulbul, and the venue for the Holy Week Healing Festival. [3, 8]
- **Cantabon Cave** (Cantabon) — 800-meter cave on the northeastern side of Mt. Bandilaan featuring crystal terraces and limestone formations. [1, 3]
- **Caticugan Marine Protected Area** (Caticugan) — Community-managed marine sanctuary for snorkeling, kayaking, paddle boating, and diving (corals, giant clams, sea turtles). [4]
- **Balay Pahauli** (Cantabon) & **San Roque Church** (Banban) — Stops on the Provincial Tourism Office’s Healing and Wellness Tour showcasing _tuob_ fumigation, herbal traditions, and _hilot_. [1, 5]
- **Secret Lagoon** (San Antonio) — Featured on the Provincial Tourism Office mountain tour. [3]

### Lazi

- **Cambugahay Falls** (Canclaran) — Three-tiered rainforest waterfall with turquoise swimming pools; Siquijor’s most visited attraction. [1–2]
- **San Isidro Labrador Parish Church and Convent** (Poblacion, Lazi) — Recognized by the **National Museum of the Philippines (2001)** as a **National Cultural Treasure** and listed on the **UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List** (_Baroque Churches of the Philippines Extension_). Built in the late 19th century (church 1884; convent completed 1891), featuring coral-stone architecture and one of the largest _conventos_ in the Visayas, home to the Siquijor Heritage Museum. [1–2, 6–7]
- **Centuries-Old Balete Tree** (Campalanas) — Ancient banyan tree estimated at nearly 500 years old with a natural cold spring and fish-spa pool at its base. [2]
- **Hapitanan** (Tignao) & **Señora River Trekking** — Viewpoint overlooking Crocodile Hill and a ~200-meter river trek listed on official tourism routes. [2, 5]

### Maria

- **Salagdoong Beach** (Olang) — White-sand cove 6 km northeast of Maria with a nearby islet. _(Note: The Provincial Tourism Office’s 2023 website states swimming was temporarily suspended pending DENR Forest Land Agreement approval; confirm current open status with the Provincial Tourism Office or LGU before visiting.)_ [2]
- **Kagusuan Beach** (Minalulan) — Quiet white-sand beach framed by coral boulders. [2–3]
- **Olang Marine Sanctuary** (Olang) — Second-largest marine protected area on the island and 2019 Isla de Fuego MPA Awards honoree. [4]
- **Our Lady of Divine Providence Parish** (Maria) — Listed heritage parish. [2]

### San Juan

- **Paliton Beach** (Paliton) — Palm-lined white-sand beach, marine protected area, and popular sunset spot. [2–3]
- **Tubod Marine Sanctuary** (Tubod) — Snorkeling and marine life sanctuary near Coco Grove Beach Resort, known for sea turtles and reefs. [4]
- **Lugnason Falls** (Napo) — Rainforest waterfall with aquamarine pools. [3]
- **Pitogo Cliff** (Tag-ibo) — Coastal rock formations, sunset spot, and marine-life viewing. [3]
- **Seashell Museum** (Tubod) & **St. Augustine Parish** (San Juan) — Marine shell exhibits and town parish. [2, 4]

### Larena

- **Larena Triad Viewpoint** (Nonoc) — Hilltop viewpoint overlooking Larena with views across Negros, Cebu, and Bohol. [2]
- **Siquijor Butterfly Garden** (Sitio Cabilao, Cang-apa) — Local butterfly conservation and breeding project. [3]
- **St. Vincent Ferrer Parish** (Larena) — Town parish. [2]

### Enrique Villanueva

- **Tulapos Marine Sanctuary and Freediving Site** (Tulapos) — Snorkeling and freediving sanctuary known for giant trevallies, barracudas, blacktip reef sharks, giant clams, and sea turtles. [4]
- **Holy Mountain of God Trek** (Cangmanki) — Hilltop pilgrimage trek with a 30-foot cross. [5]
- **Our Lady of Mount Carmel Parish** (Enrique Villanueva) — Town parish, alongside local bakery stops (_Lilibeth’s Pan Bisaya_ and _Elena’s Bakery_). [2]

## Best season for marine sanctuaries

The Provincial Tourism Office recommends planning snorkeling and dive stops by monsoon season: [4]

- **Northeast Monsoon (June–November):** Caticugan MPA (Siquijor) and Tulapos Marine Sanctuary (Enrique Villanueva).
- **Southwest Monsoon (December–May):** Olang Marine Sanctuary (Maria) and Tubod Marine Sanctuary (San Juan).

## Getting here and around

- **Sea travel:** See [Ports and sea travel](/services/tourism/ports-and-ferries) for Port of Siquijor, Port of Larena, and Port of Lazi profiles and PPA shipping-line contacts (including the Lazi–Tagbilaran–Plaridel ferry route launched 23 October 2026). [11]
- **Island transport:** Siquijor has no metered taxis or public buses. Visitors travel by **tricycle**, **jeepney/easyride** (fixed routes), **van for hire**, or **rented motorbike**. [9]

# Senior Citizen, PWD, and Solo Parent IDs

Apply for a Senior Citizen ID, Person with Disability (PWD) ID, or Solo Parent ID through your municipal hall in Siquijor, and verify your registration through national portals.

## Senior Citizen ID (OSCA)

Under **Republic Act No. 9994** (_Expanded Senior Citizens Act of 2010_), Filipino citizens aged **60 years and older** are eligible for a national Senior Citizen ID. [1]

- **Where to apply:** The **Office for Senior Citizens Affairs (OSCA)** at your municipal hall, assisted by the Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO). [1]
- **Cost and validity:** Issued **free of charge** and valid anywhere in the Philippines. [1]
- **National digital registration:** You can also register online via the **National Commission of Senior Citizens (NCSC)** Senior Citizens Data Form ([ncsc.gov.ph/seniorcitizensdataform](https://www.ncsc.gov.ph/seniorcitizensdataform)) and check the National Senior Citizens Digital ID portal ([ncsc.gov.ph/ncsid](https://www.ncsc.gov.ph/ncsid)). [2]
- **Documents to confirm locally:** Exact photo counts or local barangay-certification formats vary by municipality; confirm the local checklist with your municipal OSCA or MSWDO before visiting. See [municipal office contacts](/government/departments/office-directory).

## Person with Disability (PWD) ID

Under **RA 7277** (as amended by **RA 9442** and **RA 10754**) and **NCDA Administrative Order No. 001, s. 2021**, eligible residents with permanent disabilities—including people with cancer (RA 11215) and rare diseases (RA 10747)—apply through their municipal **MSWDO** or **Persons with Disabilities Affairs Office (PDAO)**. [3]

### Requirements for new applicants [3]

1. **Accomplished PWD ID Application Form (`PWDID-AF`)**, available from the MSWDO, PDAO, DOH, or NCDA.
2. **Confirmation of disability:**
   - **Apparent disability** (physically visible): A physician’s Certificate of Disability is **not required**; the issuing officer may assess the applicant directly (or refer to the Municipal Health Office if in doubt).
   - **Non-apparent disability** (e.g., deaf/hard of hearing, intellectual, learning, mental, psychosocial, non-apparent visual or speech impairment, cancer, or rare disease): A **Certificate of Disability** or medical certificate from an appropriate specialist or physician at a government health office or recognized medical institution.
3. **Two (2) recent 1×1 ID photos** with your name and signature or thumbmark on the back.
4. **One (1) valid government ID** (or a Barangay Certificate if unavailable; for minors, a School ID or photocopy of the Birth Certificate). Guardians or authorized representatives must bring proof of guardianship or a notarized authorization letter.
5. **Proof of residence** (Voter’s ID, Barangay Certificate, or utility bill showing your name and address).

- **Renewal or lost ID:** Submit a new `PWDID-AF` (mark Renewal) with the expired ID, or an **Affidavit of Loss** plus two 1×1 photos if lost. [3]
- **National verification:** Municipal encoders enter approved IDs into the **DOH Philippine Registry for Persons with Disability (PRPWD)** at [pwd.doh.gov.ph](https://pwd.doh.gov.ph/home.php), which also supports online ID verification. [4]

## Solo Parent ID (SPIC)

Under **Republic Act No. 11861** (_Expanded Solo Parents’ Welfare Act_), solo parents caring for unmarried, non-working dependent children **22 years old and below** (including expanded categories such as spouses of OFWs away for at least one year, legal guardians/foster parents, and pregnant women without partners) apply at their municipal **Solo Parent Office (SPO) / MSWDO**. [5–7]

### Core documentary requirements [7]

1. **Barangay certification** confirming solo parent status.
2. **Birth certificates** of dependent children.
3. **Proof of income** (for income-based benefits such as the 10% discount and VAT exemption for those earning below ₱250,000/year, or the ₱1,000 monthly LGU subsidy for minimum-wage earners and below). [5, 7]
4. **Supporting documents based on status** (e.g., death certificate of spouse, court documents for legal separation, or proof of abandonment/absence). [7]

- **Processing and validity:** DSWD states that the Solo Parent ID (SPIC) is **valid for one (1) year** and issued **within seven (7) days** from receipt of complete requirements. [6]

# Police clearance and NBI clearance

Apply online for a **National Police Clearance** at a local Siquijor police station, or prepare for an **NBI Clearance** appointment at the nearest NBI office in Dumaguete City.

## National Police Clearance System (NPCS)

The Philippine National Police processes national police clearances through [pnpclearance.ph](https://pnpclearance.ph/). [1]

### How to apply [1–2]

1. **Register or sign in** at [pnpclearance.ph](https://pnpclearance.ph/register) and complete your applicant profile.
2. **Schedule an appointment** and select your preferred police station. See [police stations in Siquijor](/services/public-safety/police-stations) for local station contacts.
3. **Pay online** via the redirected **Landbank ePayment Portal** (supports online channels as well as GCash/PayMaya/7-Eleven/Bayad Center via Cash Payment option). Save your **Payment Confirmation Slip or Electronic Official Receipt**.
4. **Appear at the selected police station** on your appointment date with:
   - **One (1) valid government-issued ID**
   - **Proof of payment / Payment Confirmation**
   - **NPCS Appointment Reference Number**
   - Complete on-site biometrics, photo, and signature capture.

### Renewals and First-Time Job Seekers [1–2]

- **Non-appearance renewal:** Applicants who completed an in-person National Police Clearance within the **last three (3) years** may use the non-appearance renewal option in the same account. [1]
- **First-Time Job Seekers (RA 11261):** Bring your **First-Time Job Seeker (FTJS) Certification** and **one (1) valid ID**. The free clearance can be availed once; first-time applicants must appear in person. [2]

**NPCS One Stop Shop support:** [(02) 8723-0401](tel:0287230401) local 7663 · [+63 927 964 6657](tel:+639279646657) (Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM). [1]

## NBI Clearance (nearest office: Dumaguete City)

### Online appointment, fees, and renewal [5–6]

- **Official portal:** [clearance.nbi.gov.ph](https://clearance.nbi.gov.ph/) (new registration, appointment scheduling, First-Time Jobseekers under RA 11261, and online verification). [5]
- **Online renewal with delivery:** Clearances issued **16 October 2016 onwards** can be renewed online with door-to-door delivery through [clearance.nbi.gov.ph](https://clearance.nbi.gov.ph/) without crossing to Dumaguete. [5]
- **Published fee:** Basic clearance fee is **₱130**, plus e-payment service charge (typically **₱25–₱30**) via GCash, Maya, 7-Eleven, Bayad Center, or online banking. Paid transactions carry a 15-day grace period. [6]

First-Time Job Seekers bring an original Barangay Certificate and signed Oath of Undertaking. [6]

# Marriage licenses, civil registry, and record corrections

Prepare for a marriage license application, request PSA marriage, death, or CENOMAR certificates, or file an administrative correction for clerical errors at your Municipal Civil Registrar in Siquijor.

## Applying for a marriage license

Under **Executive Order No. 209** (_The Family Code of the Philippines_, Articles 9–20), a marriage license is issued by the **Local Civil Registrar (LCR)** of the municipality where **either contracting party habitually resides**. [1]

### Core statutory requirements [1]

- **Separate sworn applications** filed by each party stating full name, place and date of birth, civil status, residence, citizenship, degree of relationship, and parents’ details (Art. 11).
- **Original or duly attested Birth or Baptismal Certificate** (Art. 12). If previously married, bring the deceased spouse’s **Death Certificate** or the **judicial decree** of annulment, declaration of nullity, or absolute divorce (Art. 13).
- **Ages 18 to 21 — Parental Consent (Art. 14):** Written consent of the father, mother, surviving parent, or guardian (given in person before the LCR or via notarized affidavit with two witnesses), plus a **marriage counseling certificate** (Art. 16).
- **Ages 21 to 25 — Parental Advice (Art. 15):** Sworn statement that parental advice was sought together with the written advice, plus a **marriage counseling certificate** (Art. 16). If parental advice is unfavorable or not obtained, the license is issued only after three (3) months following publication.
- **10-day posting period (Art. 17):** The LCR posts notice of the application for **10 consecutive days** outside the office before issuing the license.
- **Validity and fees (Arts. 19–20):** A marriage license is valid anywhere in the Philippines for **120 days** from issue. Prescribed local fees apply, except for **indigent parties**, who are exempt upon oath/affidavit.

Confirm any additional municipal checklists (such as CENOMAR or pre-marriage seminar schedules) with your Municipal Civil Registrar via the [office directory](/government/departments/office-directory).

## Requesting PSA marriage, death, and CENOMAR certificates

For PSA-issued security paper copies, prepare the following details listed on **PSA’s official portals** [2–4]:

- **Marriage Certificate:** Complete names of husband and wife, date and place of marriage, requester’s name and address, number of copies, and purpose. [2]
- **Death Certificate:** Complete name of deceased, date and place of death, requester’s name and address, number of copies, and purpose. [3]
- **CENOMAR (Certificate of No Marriage):** Complete name of the person, father’s complete name, mother’s complete maiden name, date and place of birth, requester’s name and address, number of copies, and purpose. [4]

**Official online ordering channels** linked from [psa.gov.ph](https://psa.gov.ph/civilregistration):

- [PSA Serbilis](https://www.psaserbilis.com.ph/)
- [PSA Helpline](https://psahelpline.ph/)

For PSA birth certificates and delivery fee details, see [Get a PSA certificate](/services/civil-documents/birth-certificates).

## Correcting clerical errors or changing a first name (RA 9048 & RA 10172)

Under **RA 9048** (as amended by **RA 10172**), your **Municipal Civil Registrar** can administratively correct—**without a court order**—[5–6]:

- Clerical or typographical errors in civil registry entries;
- Change of **first name or nickname**;
- Clerical errors in the **day and month of birth** or **sex** of a person.

_Exclusions:_ Changes involving **nationality, age (year of birth), or civil status** are not covered and require judicial proceedings. [5–6]

### Supporting documents for administrative petitions [6]

1. **Certified true copy** of the certificate or registry book page containing the error.
2. At least **two (2) public or private documents** showing the correct entry.
3. **For day/month of birth or sex corrections:** Earliest school records, medical records, or baptismal/religious documents; for sex corrections, a **certification from an accredited government physician** confirming the petitioner has not undergone sex change or transplant.
4. **Law enforcement clearance** certifying no pending case or criminal record.
5. **Newspaper publication:** Petitions for change of first name/nickname, day/month of birth, or sex must be published **once a week for two (2) consecutive weeks** in a newspaper of general circulation.

Petitions are filed in person in **three (3) copies** at the Local Civil Registry Office where the record is kept (or via migrant petition where applicable). Indigent petitioners are exempt from filing fees. [5–6]

For **late / delayed registration**, check your Municipal Civil Registrar’s documentary checklist directly, as municipal LCR checklists in Siquijor are not published online.

## Sources and reference dates

# Real property tax (Amilyar) and RSBSA agriculture registration

Check statutory due dates for paying Real Property Tax at your Municipal Treasurer’s Office, and see how Siquijor farmers and fisherfolk register in the Department of Agriculture’s RSBSA registry.

## Real Property Tax (Amilyar)

Under **Republic Act No. 7160** (_Local Government Code of 1991_), the **Municipal Treasurer** (or a deputized, bonded Barangay Treasurer) collects basic Real Property Tax (RPT) and the additional Special Education Fund (SEF) tax. [1]

### Statutory payment schedule (RA 7160, Sec. 250) [1]

Property owners may pay annual RPT and SEF tax **without interest in four (4) equal quarterly installments**:

| Quarter         | Statutory due date            |
| --------------- | ----------------------------- |
| **1st Quarter** | On or before **31 March**     |
| **2nd Quarter** | On or before **30 June**      |
| **3rd Quarter** | On or before **30 September** |
| **4th Quarter** | On or before **31 December**  |

Payments are applied first to prior years’ delinquencies, interest, and penalties before current-year taxes. [1]

### Discounts and late-payment interest [1]

- **Prompt / advance payment discount (Sec. 251):** The local sanggunian may grant a discount of **up to 20%** of the annual tax due for advance or prompt payment.
- **Delinquency interest (Sec. 255):** Unpaid taxes after the due date incur **2% interest per month** on the unpaid amount (up to a maximum of **36 months**).

_Local verification note:_ The Bureau of Local Government Finance’s CY 2026 RPT notice index does not list a published Siquijor ordinance notice. [2] Confirm the exact prompt-payment discount rate, assessment notice, and accepted payment methods directly with your **Municipal Treasurer’s Office** or **Municipal Assessor’s Office** via the [office directory](/government/departments/office-directory).

## RSBSA (Registry System for Basic Sectors in Agriculture)

The **Registry System for Basic Sectors in Agriculture (RSBSA)** is the Department of Agriculture’s official registry of farmers, farmworkers, fisherfolk, and agri-youth used to verify eligibility for government agricultural support programs. [3]

### How to register or update your record [3–4]

1. **Visit your Municipal Agriculture Office (MAO)** at your municipal hall in Siquijor.
2. **Complete the official RSBSA Enrollment Form** (available at the MAO or downloadable from [da.gov.ph/rsbsa-registration-and-updating](https://www.da.gov.ph/rsbsa-registration-and-updating/)). [3]
3. **Confirm supporting documents at the MAO** (such as a valid ID, ID photo, and proof of farming/fishing activity or land tenure) before submission; the MAO encodes verified forms into DA’s RSBSA system. [3]
4. **Verify your registration online:** Check whether your name is active in the registry using the official **DA RSBSA Finder** at [finder-rsbsa.da.gov.ph](https://finder-rsbsa.da.gov.ph/) (search by full name, sex, and date of birth). [4]

2. [Bureau of Local Government Finance — Notices of Payment of RPT and SEF Tax of LGUs for CY 2026](https://blgf.gov.ph/notices-of-payment-of-real-property-tax-and-special-education-fund-tax-of-lgus-for-cy-2026/), CY 2026, checked 21 November 2026.
